report.headline_answer: Live remeasure preserved the finding. The monitor reports LIVE, UNVERIFIED, CLOSED, and UNVERIFIED across the four truths. Finished vs stalled is distinct via closed_at. Dead-monitor live work and genuine stall share admitted inputs and both stay UNVERIFIED. classify() has no mtime read.

extensions.question_or_target: Does the monitor correctly distinguish these four states - work running with monitor alive, work running with monitor dead, work finished, and work genuinely stalled - or does it conflate any pair?
extensions.answer: It returns LIVE, UNVERIFIED, CLOSED, and UNVERIFIED. It distinguishes the plainly-running and explicit-finish states and avoids a false-dead verdict, but conflates dead heartbeat monitoring with genuine stall because both expose stale heartbeat plus held process lock. UNVERIFIED is the honest answer until orchestrator progress state is added.

enumerated_targets.claim: The monitor emits four distinct classifications for four truths.
Live work is reported DEAD when its heartbeat monitor dies.
An explicit 11-hour-old finish is distinguished from an idle-sleep stall.
Dead heartbeat monitoring with live work and genuine stall have the same admitted signal values and are structurally undecidable.
The classifier infers a state from file mtimes alone.

signal_source_audit.process: kernel fcntl.flock contention/release; not file mtime
